From 9f235ccecd03c436cb1683eac16b12f119e54aa9 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Matt Johnston <matt@codeconstruct.com.au>
Date: Tue, 13 Jan 2026 17:41:34 +0800
Subject: [PATCH] ipmi: ipmb: initialise event handler read bytes

IPMB doesn't use i2c reads, but the handler needs to set a value.
Otherwise an i2c read will return an uninitialised value from the bus
driver.

Fixes: 63c4eb347164 ("ipmi:ipmb: Add initial support for IPMI over IPMB")
Signed-off-by: Matt Johnston <matt@codeconstruct.com.au>
Message-ID: <20260113-ipmb-read-init-v1-1-a9cbce7b94e3@codeconstruct.com.au>
Signed-off-by: Corey Minyard <corey@minyard.net>

diff --git a/drivers/char/ipmi/ipmi_ipmb.c b/drivers/char/ipmi/ipmi_ipmb.c
index 3a51e58b2487..28818952a7a4 100644
--- a/drivers/char/ipmi/ipmi_ipmb.c
+++ b/drivers/char/ipmi/ipmi_ipmb.c
@@ -202,11 +202,16 @@ static int ipmi_ipmb_slave_cb(struct i2c_client *client,
 		break;
 
 	case I2C_SLAVE_READ_REQUESTED:
+		*val = 0xff;
+		ipmi_ipmb_check_msg_done(iidev);
+		break;
+
 	case I2C_SLAVE_STOP:
 		ipmi_ipmb_check_msg_done(iidev);
 		break;
 
 	case I2C_SLAVE_READ_PROCESSED:
+		*val = 0xff;
 		break;
 	}
 
-- 
2.34.1

## Summary

The patch fixes an uninitialized value issue in the IPMI IPMB driver (`drivers/char/ipmi/ipmi_ipmb.c`).  

**Modifications in the file:**  
- In function `ipmi_ipmb_slave_cb`, the `I2C_SLAVE_READ_REQUESTED` case is now handled separately from `I2C_SLAVE_STOP`. It writes the byte `0xff` into the read buffer (`*val`) and also calls `ipmi_ipmb_check_msg_done()`.  
- The `I2C_SLAVE_READ_PROCESSED` case now writes `0xff` into `*val`.  
- The `I2C_SLAVE_STOP` case remains unchanged (only calls `ipmi_ipmb_check_msg_done()`).

**Relationships:**  
The IPMB protocol does not use i2c reads, but the i2c slave callback can still be invoked for read operations. Previously, the driver left the read buffer uninitialized, which could return stale or kernel stack data. By explicitly writing `0xff`, the patch ensures a safe default value is returned. The separation of the `I2C_SLAVE_READ_REQUESTED` case also ensures the message completion check is performed immediately after the read request, rather than only at stop. Together, these changes prevent uninitialized memory exposure and align the callback behavior with the driver's intended operation.
